text: Tengrism is a faith of the Eurasian steppes, the wide lands of the Turkic and Mongolic peoples.
Tengrists honour Tengri, the eternal blue sky, with the earth mother and many other gods and spirits.
src: a belief system that arose on the Eurasian steppes / It formed from the folk religions of the Turkic and Mongolic peoples
Tengrism centres on Tengri, the eternal blue sky, with the earth mother and many other gods and spirits

text: More than 2,300 years ago, Chinese writers recorded Tengri as the sky god of the Xiongnu people.
Later it was the faith of the Göktürks, the Bulgars, the Khazars and the Mongol Empire.
src: Chinese chronicles first record Tengri as the sky god of the Xiongnu in the 4th century BCE
It was the faith of the Xiongnu, the Göktürks, the Bulgars, the Khazars and the Mongol Empire

text: Old writings called the Orkhon inscriptions say that the khans, the rulers, acted because “Heaven so ordained”.
In Tengrist belief, people are the children of Father Heaven and Mother Earth.
src: The Orkhon inscriptions in Old Turkic script record that the khagans acted because “Heaven so ordained”
Humans are the children of Father Heaven and Mother Earth

text: A book called the Secret History of the Mongols, written in 1240, names Tengri many times.
Genghis Khan and the khans after him followed Tengri, but they were open to other faiths.
src: The Secret History of the Mongols, written in 1240, names Tengri many times
Genghis Khan and several generations of his successors were Tengrist “shaman-kings”, open to other faiths

text: More than 600 years ago, most Turkic and Mongol peoples began to turn to Islam and Buddhism.
But Tengrist ideas lived on inside the faiths that took its place.
src: Turkic and Mongol peoples largely turned to Islam and Buddhism from the 14th century
Tengrist ideas survived inside the faiths that replaced it

text: Since the 1990s, a new form of Tengrism has grown in Central Asia and Siberia.
Today more than one million people in Kazakhstan follow it.
src: since the 1990s Tengrism has been revived in Central Asia and Siberia, a modern and monotheistic movement distinct from the historical religion
